recipe_inventory.label: Adireddy et al. (2010): Open-atmosphere precursor mixing

source_locators.locator: SI PDF p. 2, Chemicals and synthesis of cube-like BaTiO3 nanoparticles

recipe_inventory.scope: Open-atmosphere precursor mixing; 20 nm applies only to regular-cube subset.
gaps: Complete three-page main and matched ten-page SI, all three main and seven SI figures and 28 numbered main references. Cited full sources unreviewed.

Addition order and rate among the four solutions, mixing time, temperature ramp, hot pressure, centrifuge speed/time, purification details and toluene volume are not reported. Natural cooling to room temperature is explicit.
Open-atmosphere and anaerobic glovebox solution preparation are separate source routes; the glovebox atmosphere identity is unknown. SI explicitly assigns the same hydrothermal treatment to both.
Acetic-acid wash is a separate post-treatment of carbonate-containing powder: 5% is printed without basis, wash volume/time or independently reported final particle size.
Yield 85–90% is reported for the method without atmosphere-specific allocation. No size selection was performed.

The 20 nm TEM value describes only the 36% regular-cube subset of air-prepared particles. The approximately 58% cube-like and 6% truncated populations are distinct observations, not three new preparations.

HRTEM Figure S2, FTIR Figure S5 (caption 21.5 nm), TGA/DSC and optical curves are not given an exact physical-batch crosswalk. Their support records do not inherit all direct-route conditions or produce extra pairs.
No measured atomic coordinates are supplied. Pseudocubic cell indexing and interpreted local distortions are not a measured atomic model; neutron/PFM investigations are described as ongoing.
Independent source comparison passed; molecular/particle/reference-cell presentation remains pending.

source_notes.label: Atmosphere precedes sealed heating
source_notes.summary: Open-atmosphere mixing gives mixed cube-like populations and carbonate impurity; anaerobic glovebox mixing gives regular cubes. Both source treatments use 135 °C for18 h; the glovebox gas and hot pressure are unknown.
source_locators: SI PDF p. 2, Chemicals and synthesis of cube-like BaTiO3 nanoparticles

source_notes.label: Shape and phase are separate
source_notes.summary: Regular-cube shape does not uniquely establish a cubic polymorph. XRD uses a pseudocubic assumption while Raman indicates local tetragonal distortions; no measured atomic coordinates are supplied.

source_notes.label: Size populations and aliquots
source_notes.summary: 20 nm is the air-route regular-cube subset;22 nm is the inert-route average edge;21.3 nm is Scherrer size. The separate21.5 nm FTIR caption and4.09 Å HRTEM spacing retain their own sample qualifications.

source_notes.label: Source notation conflicts
source_notes.summary: The optical excitation-energy parentheticals and some SI instrument/range statements are inconsistent as printed. They are retained as qualified context, without guessed corrections.

evidence_conflicts.summary: Main p.3 pairs excitation 390 nm with 2.43 eV and 510 nm with printed 3.18 nm. Wavelengths are retained; the inconsistent energy/unit parentheticals are not corrected or used as energy measurements.

evidence_conflicts.summary: Main p.2 assumes pseudocubic indexing because cubic and tetragonal polymorphs cannot be resolved by these XRD data; Raman supports local tetragonal distortions. Cubic particle morphology does not establish a uniquely refined cubic phase.
